2607.20092.title: ENTRAP-VL: A Taxonomic Probe for Dual Contextual Entrainment in Vision-Language Models
2607.20092.paper_summary: Contextual entrainment is the tendency of a model to let auxiliary context in its input pull its output, independently of whether that context is relevant, true, or even meaningful. Recently, it has been identified and given a mechanistic account in unimodal language models. Whether and how it manifests in vision-language models (VLMs) is, by contrast, largely unexamined, and the field lacks a purpose-built instrument with which to investigate it. We take the position that studying contextual entrainment in VLMs requires more than porting an existing text-only benchmark to the multimodal setting: it requires a taxonomically structured, dual-modality instrument whose conditions are constructed around the item at hand (the depicted image in the textual stream, the textual query in the visual stream). We argue that the move to VLMs is substantive rather than incremental. It makes entrainment a dual phenomenon, drivable independently by textual and by visual context, and it opens a veracity distinction (context that is false of the depicted scene yet possible in the world) that has no counterpart in the unimodal, world-knowledge-only formulation of prior work. To make this position concrete and actionable, we introduce ENTRAP-VL (ENTRainment Assessment Probe for Vision and Language), a manually curated dataset of 1,500 items across eight categories, organized by a taxonomy that spans two axes, i.e., the association of context with the item and its relationship to truth, and split into a textual-entrainment stream (eight context conditions) and a visual-entrainment stream (three context conditions). We do not claim to measure entrainment in any particular model; we provide the instrument, the taxonomy that motivates it, and the evaluation protocols it enables, so that the community can investigate the phenomenon rigorously. We will release the dataset and its documentation publicly.
2607.20092.paper_summary_zh: 上下文的引導是模型讓輸入中的輔助上下文影響其輸出的趨勢，無論該上下文是否相關、真實或甚至有意義。最近，這一現象在單模態語言模型中被識別並給予了機械性解釋。相比之下，它在視覺-語言模型（VLMs）中的表現如何以及是否存在，則大多未被檢視，該領域缺乏一個專門設計的工具來進行調查。我們認為，在VLMs中研究上下文引導需要的不僅僅是將現有的純文本基準移植到多模態環境中：它需要一個分類結構化的雙模態工具，其條件圍繞當前項目構建（文本流中的描繪圖像，視覺流中的文本查詢）。我們主張，轉向VLMs是實質性的而非漸進式的。這使得引導成為一種雙重現象，可以獨立地由文本和視覺上下文驅動，並且開啟了一個真實性區分（對於描繪場景而言是虛假的上下文，但在世界上可能存在），這在以往的單模態、僅基於世界知識的研究中是沒有對應的。為了使這一立場具體且可操作，我們介紹了ENTRAP-VL（視覺與語言的引導評估探針），這是一個手動策劃的數據集，包含1,500個項目，分為八個類別，並根據兩個軸的分類法進行組織，即上下文與項目的關聯及其與真實的關係，並分為文本引導流（八個上下文條件）和視覺引導流（三個上下文條件）。我們並不聲稱在任何特定模型中測量引導；我們提供工具、激勵其的分類法和它所啟用的評估協議，以便社群能夠嚴謹地研究這一現象。我們將公開發布數據集及其文檔。
